skill.name: assume-cloudformation-role
skill.description: Assumes an AWS IAM role for CloudFormation work and prepares temporary AWS CLI credentials for stack operations.
skill.summary: Prepare temporary AWS credentials for CloudFormation stack operations.
skill.author: Daisuke897

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate DevOps helper, but it obtains and exports AWS STS credentials for CloudFormation operations. Key risks include predictable temporary credential storage, environment variable exposure, a hard-coded role ARN, and destructive stack examples. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp with restrictive permissions, avoid shared paths, and delete the file with a trap on exit.
Prefer AWS CLI profiles, process-local environment scope, and explicit credential unset steps after the task.
Require the user to provide profile, role ARN, account, and region before any assume-role command.
Require confirmation and change review before create, update, or delete stack operations.

content.value_statement: CloudFormation work often fails when temporary role credentials are missing. This skill guides AWS STS role assumption and environment setup for CLI-based stack operations.
actual_capabilities: Runs an AWS STS assume-role workflow using a named AWS CLI profile.
Shows how to export temporary AccessKeyId, SecretAccessKey, and SessionToken values.
Uses jq to parse credential fields from the STS response.
Removes the temporary credential file after environment variables are set.
Lists example create, update, and delete commands for CloudFormation stacks.
limitations: Requires AWS CLI, jq, and a local AWS profile with sts:AssumeRole permission.
Defaults contain a specific profile and role ARN that must be reviewed before use.
Uses a predictable /tmp credentials file in the provided example.
Does not validate templates, stack policies, regions, or IAM blast radius.

use_cases.title: Prepare Stack Credentials
use_cases.description: Set up temporary credentials before creating or updating a CloudFormation stack from a local workstation.

use_cases.title: Review Credential Workflow
use_cases.description: Inspect the assume-role process and improve how temporary credentials are handled during automation.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Credential Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the role assumption workflow for safer temporary credential handling. Recommend changes that reduce secret exposure without changing the deployment goal.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It prepares temporary AWS credentials by assuming an IAM role for CloudFormation operations.

faq.question: Does it deploy stacks automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides credential setup and examples. Stack operations still need explicit user direction.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: The workflow requires AWS CLI, jq, and an AWS profile with permission to assume the target role.

faq.question: Can I use a different role ARN?
faq.answer: Yes. Review and replace the default profile, role ARN, and session name before use.

faq.question: Why are temporary credentials risky?
faq.answer: They can grant AWS access until expiration, especially if exposed through files, logs, or inherited environments.

faq.question: How should I use it safely?
faq.answer: Verify the account, region, stack name, and permissions before running any CloudFormation command.
